findings.title: Coverage — read this first
findings.text: The path library holds 104 windows with recorded price paths (104 partial — RIPTIDE-seeded windows polled late, 2026-11-17→19; the rest full from the pathwatch start). Families below are counted from those paths only. The ledger scan covers every graded window the desk has sealed, path or no path. Selection warning: every partial-path window is one RIPTIDE seeded on — a parent had already called it — so family hit rates are conditional on that and read higher than an all-windows rate would. Full-coverage windows carry no such filter.

findings.title: Everyone-loses windows (the prime family)
findings.text: Of 13 path windows where PLAIN, EARLY and the caller majority all took a side, 2 (15.4%) ended with ALL of them wrong. These windows are tagged in the library; their WHY labels are the first thing to study.

findings.title: Flip anatomy
findings.text: 8 windows flipped: a side led at a median 0.818 mid before the 240s mark and still lost. The final break (last 50c cross) came at a median 251.5s. 2 of 8 carried a late-fire label (winner's mid +0.20 or more in the final minute); 1 carried a BTC-lurch label (spot moved 0.15%+ inside the window).

findings.title: One-turners
findings.text: 16 one-turners: quiet first (median pre-move range 0.12), then one move of a median 0.45 mid points at a median 227.0s in, and no cross-back after. The seconds before the step are where the WHY hunt concentrates.

findings.title: Chop vs clean — is confusion itself the tell?
findings.text: CHOP windows: 7 (median 4 crosses of 50c). In chop, PLAIN hit no counted calls (n=0) and the crowd 100.0% (n=7). In CLEAN windows (35), PLAIN hit 100.0% (n=5) and the crowd 97.0% (n=33). If chop accuracy sits near coin-flip while clean accuracy holds, the confusion is the signal — the numbers above are the verdict, whichever way they land.

findings.title: Everyone-loses, ledger-wide
findings.text: Across all sealed graded windows where PLAIN, EARLY and the caller majority all have grades (244 windows), all three were wrong together 7 times (2.9%). That is the base rate the flip family has to beat to mean anything.

findings.title: When windows actually break
findings.text: Of 40 path windows with a final 50c cross, the decision point (last cross) sat at a median 237.0s, and 19 (47.5%) broke in the final minute. Anything decided before that is path, not decision.
